How New Species Evolve
¨Reproductive Isolating Mechanisms (cont.)
¨Postzygotic Isolating Mechanisms-Prevent hybrid offspring from developing or breeding
¤Hybrid Inviability-hybrid zygote is not viable and dies
¤Hybrid Sterility -hybrid zygote develops into a sterile adult
explanation: Postzygotic Isolating Mechanisms are reproductive barriers that act after fertilization has occurred, preventing hybrid offspring from successfully developing or reproducing. The slide details two main types: (1) Hybrid Inviability, where the hybrid zygote is genetically incompatible, fails to develop properly, and dies; and (2) Hybrid Sterility, where the hybrid zygote successfully develops into an adult, but the adult is sterile (unable to produce gametes/offspring), thereby halting further gene flow between the parent species.

questions.q: What is the difference between hybrid inviability and hybrid sterility?
opts: Hybrid inviability occurs before fertilization; hybrid sterility occurs after fertilization.
Hybrid inviability means the hybrid zygote dies; hybrid sterility means the hybrid develops into a sterile adult.
Hybrid inviability occurs in plants; hybrid sterility occurs in animals.
Hybrid inviability leads to polyploidy; hybrid sterility leads to genetic drift.
questions.exp: Hybrid inviability refers to the death of the hybrid zygote, while hybrid sterility refers to the hybrid successfully growing into an adult but being unable to reproduce.
